q: A thread is:
choices: A basic unit of CPU utilization
explain: **A thread is a basic unit of CPU utilization**.

q: A thread comprises all of the following EXCEPT:
choices: A register set and a stack
explain: الـ thread ليه: **thread ID, program counter, register set, stack**. أما الـ **code section** فمشترك بين كل الـ threads في الـ process.

q: Threads belonging to the same process share:
choices: Code section, data section, and OS resources such as open files and signals
explain: بيشاركوا **code section, data section, OS resources (open files, signals)**.

q: Which of the following is private to each thread (NOT shared)?
explain: الـ **stack** (ومعاه registers و program counter و thread ID) خاص بكل thread.

q: In a multithreaded process, which items appear once and are shared by all threads in the diagram?
explain: في شكل الـ multithreaded process: **code, data, files** مرة واحدة فوق، و**registers و stack** لكل thread.

q: A program that cannot draw pictures while reading keystrokes illustrates the need for:
explain: الحل المثالي إن **جزئين من البرنامج يتنفذوا في نفس الوقت**، والـ **Threads** هي اللي بتسمح بده.

q: A web browser where one thread displays images while another retrieves data from the network is an example of:
explain: ده مثال **multithreaded application**: process واحدة فيها كذا thread of control.

q: In the word processor example, which task is performed by a background thread?
explain: Word processor: thread للجرافيكس، و thread للكيبورد، و **thread تالت للـ spelling and grammar checking في الخلفية**.

q: Most software applications that run on modern computers are:
explain: **Most software applications that run on modern computers are multithreaded**.

q: An application is typically implemented as:
choices: A separate process with several threads of control
explain: **An application typically is implemented as a separate process with several threads of control**.

q: In a multithreaded server architecture, after receiving a client request the server:
choices: Stops listening until the request is complete
Creates a new process for every byte
Creates a new thread to service the request and resumes listening for additional requests
explain: (1) request ← (2) **create new thread to service the request** ← (3) **resume listening for additional client requests**.

q: Most operating-system kernels today are:
choices: Multithreaded, each thread performing a specific task
explain: **Most OS kernels are now multithreaded**: كل thread بيعمل مهمة معينة (devices, memory, interrupt handling).

q: Which is an example of a task performed by a kernel thread?
explain: Kernel threads بتعمل مهام زي **managing devices, managing memory, interrupt handling**.

q: Multithreaded programming provides a mechanism for more efficient use of:
explain: **Multithreaded programming provides a mechanism for more efficient use of multicore or multiprocessor systems**.

q: On a single-core system, threads T1 to T4 interleaving over time is called:
explain: على **single-core** الـ threads بتتبادل، وده **concurrent execution**. أما الـ parallelism فمحتاج multi-core.

q: Threads running at the same instant on core 1 and core 2 is an example of:
explain: **Parallelism on a multi-core system**: T1 و T2 بيتنفذوا فعلًا في نفس اللحظة على cores مختلفة.

q: Which statement is TRUE?
choices: Parallelism is possible on a single core
explain: ممكن يبقى فيه **concurrency من غير parallelism** (single-core بيتبادل). لكن الـ parallelism محتاج أكتر من core.

q: Threads supported above the kernel and managed without kernel support are:
explain: **User threads are supported above the kernel and are managed without kernel support**.

q: Threads supported and managed directly by the operating system are:
explain: **Kernel threads are supported and managed directly by the operating system**.

q: The three common models relating user threads and kernel threads are:
explain: **the one-to-one model, the many-to-one model, and the many-to-many model**.

q: The one-to-one model maps:
choices: Each user thread to a kernel thread
Many user threads to one kernel thread
Many user threads to many kernel threads
Each kernel thread to many processes
explain: **The one-to-one model maps each user thread to a kernel thread**.

q: A key advantage of the one-to-one model is that it:
choices: Allows multiple threads to run in parallel on multiprocessors
Allows only one thread at a time
explain: **It also allows multiple threads to run in parallel on multiprocessors**.

q: The only drawback of the one-to-one model is that:
choices: A blocking call blocks the entire process
Creating a user thread requires creating the corresponding kernel thread
It cannot be used on Linux
explain: **The only drawback: creating a user thread requires creating the corresponding kernel thread**، والـ overhead ده ممكن يتقّل الأداء.

q: Because of the overhead of creating kernel threads, most implementations of the one-to-one model:
choices: Restrict the number of threads supported by the system
explain: **Most implementations of this model restrict the number of threads supported by the system**.

q: Which operating systems implement the one-to-one model?
explain: **Linux, along with the family of Windows operating systems, implement the one-to-one model**.

q: In the many-to-one model:
choices: Each user thread has its own kernel thread
Many user threads are mapped to a single kernel thread
Many kernel threads map to one user thread
explain: **Many-to-One**: كذا user thread متربطين بـ **kernel thread واحد**.

q: In the many-to-one model, if one thread makes a blocking system call:
choices: Only that thread blocks and others continue
A new kernel thread is created
explain: لأن فيه **kernel thread واحد بس**، لو thread عمل blocking call **الـ process كلها تقف**.

q: Why can't threads in the many-to-one model run in parallel on a multicore system?
choices: They are created by the hardware
Only one thread can access the kernel at a time
explain: مفيش غير **kernel thread واحد**، فـ **thread واحد بس** يقدر يتجدول على الـ kernel في كل مرة، فمفيش true concurrency.

q: The many-to-many model:
choices: Allows many user-level threads to be mapped to many kernel threads
Maps each user thread to one kernel thread
Maps all user threads to one kernel thread
explain: **Allows many user level threads to be mapped to many kernel threads**.

q: Which model allows the operating system to create a sufficient number of kernel threads?
explain: **Many-to-Many: Allows the operating system to create a sufficient number of kernel threads**.

q: In the many-to-many model, the developer can create:
choices: Exactly as many user threads as CPU cores
As many user threads as he or she wishes
explain: **Allows the developer to create as many user threads as she wishes**.

q: The two-level model is similar to many-to-many, except that it:
choices: Maps each kernel thread to the disk
Allows a user thread to be bound to a kernel thread
explain: **Two-level: Similar to Many-to-Many, except that it allows a user thread to be bound to kernel thread**.

q: In the two-level model diagram, one user thread on the right is connected directly to its own kernel thread. This is called being:
explain: الـ user thread اللي متربط بـ kernel thread لوحده اسمه **bound**.

q: Which model provides the LEAST parallelism on a multiprocessor?
explain: الـ **Many-to-One** فيه kernel thread واحد بس، فمفيش parallelism خالص.

q: Which model has the highest overhead per user thread because each one needs its own kernel thread?
explain: الـ **One-to-One**: كل user thread محتاج kernel thread، وده overhead.

q: Which benefit of threads allows continued execution if part of a process is blocked, especially important for user interfaces?
explain: **Responsiveness – may allow continued execution if part of process is blocked, especially important for user interfaces**.

q: 'Threads share resources of the process, easier than shared memory or message passing' describes:
explain: ده **Resource Sharing**.

q: 'Cheaper than process creation; thread switching has lower overhead than context switching' describes:
explain: ده **Economy**.

q: 'A process can take advantage of multiprocessor architectures' describes:
explain: ده **Scalability**.

q: Which is NOT one of the four benefits of threads listed in the lecture?
explain: الفوائد الأربعة: **Responsiveness, Resource Sharing, Economy, Scalability**. والـ Security مش منهم.

q: Compared with creating a new process, creating a new thread is:
explain: الـ thread **cheaper than process creation** (Economy)، لأنه بيشارك الموارد بدل ما ياخد نسخة جديدة.

q: A thread library provides the programmer with:
choices: An API for creating and managing threads
explain: **Thread library provides programmer with API for creating and managing threads**.

q: The three main thread libraries in use today are:
explain: **POSIX Pthreads, Windows, and Java**.

q: Pthreads is the thread library associated with:
explain: **POSIX Pthreads** للأنظمة المبنية على POSIX زي UNIX و Linux.

q: Compared with processes, switching between threads of the same process is:
explain: **Thread switching lower overhead than context switching** بين processes، لأن الـ threads بتشارك نفس الـ address space.

q: Each thread has its own stack because:
choices: Each thread calls its own functions with its own local variables and return addresses
The kernel requires it for booting
explain: الـ stack فيه **local variables و function parameters و return addresses**، وكل thread بينادي functions مختلفة، فلازم يبقى ليه stack لوحده.

q: Which statement best describes the relationship between user threads and kernel threads?
choices: Kernel threads run only in user space
Ultimately, a relationship must exist between them
explain: **Ultimately, a relationship must exist between user threads and kernel threads**، وده اللي بتوصفه الـ multithreading models.

q: The main reason a server creates a new thread for each request is to:
choices: Use less memory than a single request
Serve many clients at the same time while continuing to listen
explain: الـ server بيدّي كل طلب لـ thread ويرجع **يسمع لطلبات تانية** على طول، فيخدم عملاء كتير في نفس الوقت.

q: Which model allows the developer to create many user threads AND still achieve parallel execution on a multiprocessor?
explain: الـ **Many-to-Many**: user threads كتير، والـ kernel threads المتعددة تقدر تشتغل بالتوازي.

q: In the 'Parallelism on a multi-core system' figure, core 1 executes T1 and T3 while core 2 executes:
explain: في الشكل: **core 1 ← T1, T3** و **core 2 ← T2, T4** بالتوازي.
